CHIEF COMPLAINT
Nonhealing foot ulcer

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports nonhealing foot ulcer for approximately two months. Recent onset of redness and drainage. Patient believes injury occurred from walking barefoot on Dewey Beach. Describes occasional throbbing sensation without specific localized pain. Primary care physician prescribed antibiotics prior to this visit, which patient has not yet picked up. Patient cannot recall the specific antibiotic name but reports taking it previously.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever. Reports occasional throbbing in foot.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Diabetes mellitus. Patient reports taking diabetes medication but does not regularly monitor blood glucose levels. Last A1C approximately 10.

MEDICATIONS
Diabetes medication (type not specified).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works in an ambulance. Injury sustained while walking barefoot on Dewey Beach.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs normal, afebrile. Right foot examination reveals a 1 x 2 inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral foot proximal to the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint. Redness, drainage, and edema present. Fluid drainage noted. No necrosis, no odor, no bony exposure. On palpation, increased pressure sensation reported without distinct pain.

RESULTS
X-ray of right foot: No evidence of osteomyelitis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Diabetic foot ulcer with infection. Ankle brachial index ordered to assess blood supply. Debridement performed. Clindamycin 400 mg orally twice daily for 7 days prescribed for infection. Surgical shoe provided for one month to reduce pressure. Follow-up appointment in two weeks with possible additional debridement depending on tissue appearance. Patient instructed to call office with any concerns between visits. Patient advised to seek urgent care or emergency room evaluation if develops fever or other emergency symptoms. Patient instructed to follow up with primary care physician for diabetes management as A1C of approximately 10 is elevated.
